channel.title: The Wall Street Journal - CIO Journal
channel.description: Technology leadership and enterprise technology news from CIO Journal

item.title: The Best Boards in America Are Helping Drive AI Strategy
item.description: The Oct. 23 Morning Download looks at how companies ranked high in the WSJ Leadership Institute's Best Boards 2026 list are shaping AI strategy, from Lam Research's board-backed chief AI officer and innovation committee to eBay's three-member technology committee and Trimble's board built around tech, risk and capital-allocation "archetypes." Lumentum board chair Penny Herscher said one director worked as an employee for three months to help on supply chain, calling it "a more engaged board than I've ever worked on before." At Nasdaq, chief strategy officer Jeremy Skule said directors track a dashboard of AI measures, including agents deployed and revenue delivered, and advise on token costs.
item.dc:creator: Belle Lin

item.title: Barclays Cuts 5% of Jobs In AI Overhaul
item.description: The Oct. 22 Morning Download leads with Barclays cutting 5,000 jobs, about 5% of its workforce, as it builds AI deeper into the bank; CEO C.S. Venkatakrishnan said roughly 60% of the cuts hit support functions, "including fewer developers as AI makes our people more productive," and the newsletter notes HSBC and Standard Chartered are planning similar reductions. At Gartner's IT Symposium/Xpo, analyst Tina Nunno cast CIOs as the "adult supervision" against AI hype, saying boards can be "potentially part of the problem." The roundup also covers Meta raising its 2026 capital spending floor to $135 billion and the AI-discovered PHP vulnerability that sent web administrators scrambling.
item.dc:creator: Steven Rosenbush

item.title: AI Drives Record Growth in Information Technology
item.description: Gartner forecasts worldwide IT spending will jump a record 15% to $7.3 trillion in 2027, led by 55% growth in data center systems, while the scramble for memory and chips pushes conventional server prices up about 120% by 2027. For CIOs facing hardware costs, Gartner analyst John-David Lovelock warned, "they've not seen anything yet, and there is no relief coming." The Morning Download also covers Gartner's 2027 technology trends, which reflect what analyst Gene Alvarez calls "an age of caution" in enterprise AI, and a draft Anthropic IPO prospectus showing nearly $9 billion in first-half compute spending.
item.dc:creator: Tom Loftus

item.title: AI’s Transformational Value Remains Elusive for Most Companies
item.description: A Gartner survey of 2,002 CIOs and technology executives found just 13% say their organizations have realized significant or transformational value from AI, even as 58% report rising pressure to deliver AI cost improvements. Gartner says a "vanguard" of CIOs pulls ahead by setting stopping rules for both pilots and production projects and planning role redesigns for a human-agent workforce, with analyst Alicia Mullery describing "a wide gap" between the AI innovation race and the AI outcomes race. The Morning Download also covers UAE-based CNTXT AI's expansion into Milpitas, Calif., and a DHS order for federal agencies to remove DeepSeek products.
item.dc:creator: Tom Loftus

item.title: U.A.E.-Based AI and Data Startup Expands Into Silicon Valley
item.description: CNTXT AI, a U.A.E.-based startup that builds Arabic-first AI models such as the Munsit voice AI and supplies training data to hyperscalers, is opening its first U.S. office in Milpitas, Calif., after a $60 million Series A in June. CEO Mohammad Abu Sheikh, 25, says the company has $300 million in committed revenue, mostly from U.S. customers, and sees the Middle East's large blue-collar workforce as a source of real-world data for training robots that still struggle with tasks like folding a T-shirt. He describes the U.S.-Middle East relationship as moving from buyer and seller to "a complete partnership cycle."
item.dc:creator: Steven Rosenbush

item.title: Jamie Dimon Tells Leaders to Ramp Up Cyber Defenses
item.description: The Morning Download leads with JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon telling Alan Murray that cybersecurity, with powerful new AI models, is now the bank's "biggest risk by far," alongside concerns about undersea cables, critical infrastructure and vendor supply chains. Dimon urged companies to start immediately on network segmentation, identity access management and AI-driven vulnerability hunting, and to make fast patching a regular management-meeting item. The newsletter also previews a tech earnings week with Meta, IBM and SAP reporting Wednesday and notes Microsoft pulled out of a U.K. data-center lease with Nscale.
item.dc:creator: Steven Rosenbush

item.title: Nvidia-Backed Startup doubleAI Launches Model to Pare Cost of Compute
item.description: Tel Aviv startup doubleAI, co-founded by Mobileye's Amnon Shashua and backed by Nvidia, Dell and others with $220 million raised, is launching what it calls "code execution models" that sit inside running programs and make GPU and CPU code run more efficiently without human involvement. Its first model, Maxwell, cut one early customer's compute costs by 67%, and the roughly 40-person company plans to charge a share of what customers save. Shashua expects the biggest gains for AI labs with huge training and inference bills, and the startup spent about half its funding on 1,000 Nvidia B300 chips because "you cannot rely just on renting compute."
item.dc:creator: Belle Lin

item.title: Nvidia, Meta and Apple Unveil New Open Models
item.description: The Morning Download reports that Nvidia released three new open models in its Nemotron family on Thursday, including Nemotron 3.5 Super VL for always-on AI agents, which can also handle images and video, while Meta announced a new open-weight model it will run locally on high-end Macs with Apple. Nvidia's Kari Briski said demand is rising because the models are U.S.-made with inspectable data, and companies including Atlassian, CrowdStrike and Salesforce have customized them with their own data. Briski called the releases "a message to developers and our partners and enterprises that they can depend on us."
item.dc:creator: Belle Lin

item.title: Bloomberg CEO’s ‘Aggressive’ Stance on AI
item.description: The Morning Download leads with Bloomberg CEO Vlad Kliatchko, whose company has opened its ASKB conversational AI interface to all Terminal users and who says "it's premature to focus on the ROI" of an aggressive AI investment. Kliatchko added that AI has vindicated Bloomberg's spending on journalism, since original news is now one of its most valuable assets. The newsletter also covers a tech stock selloff led by CoreWeave and rising concern about AI companies' trade secrets, including OpenAI's filing accusing a former employee who returned to Apple of taking confidential device files.
item.dc:creator: Steven Rosenbush

item.title: AI Fuels M&A Machine
item.description: With IPOs stalled despite $515.8 billion in U.S. venture dealmaking through the third quarter, Steven Rosenbush writes that "The M&A door is open" for AI startups. His examples include Amazon's talks to buy Decart for about $7 billion, Nvidia's early talks to deepen its investment in Reflection AI and IonQ's all-stock deal for cybersecurity firm Elisity, valued at up to $1.3 billion. The newsletter also cites Apollo economist Torsten Slok's view that AI's productivity payoff "remains a forecast rather than an observation."
item.dc:creator: Steven Rosenbush
